missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-predictable-quadratic-variation-C010 (partial): The worked boundary and the full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p15.finite-variation-convergence) are missing for one claim the entry makes about itself, at body lines 182-183: that stopping before the next variance increment is essential to the bound A_{T_c and n} <= c. No line gives an example or argument showing that the bound fails, or that the localization breaks, if one stops instead at the first exceedance inf{n: A_n > c}. Annex lines 234-261 prove only the positive bound and the convergence claims. The citation attached to that sentence (thm. 4.5.2, printed p. 240 of the held Durrett Version 5) only uses this stopping device. It neither states nor shows that the device is necessary.

sections.title: Density martingales, likelihood products and absolute continuity

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-density-martingales-and-product-measures-C012 (partial): The construction or argument and the full treatment promised by proved=annex:p15.product-gaussian-comparison are missing for the promised case 'singular otherwise' (body handbook/parts/p15/density-martingales-and-product-measures.tex l.237-238). The annex (handbook/annex/p15/density-martingales-and-product-measures.tex l.362-363) derives that assertion only from 'the affinity series criterion and its reverse-measure conclusion'. As stated, thm:p15-product-affinity-series gives only mu<<nu iff sum(1-h_m)<infinity, and the reverse-measure conclusion gives only nu<<mu. Neither yields mu perp nu when sum(1-h_m)=infinity. The step sum(1-h_m)=infinity => H_infinity=0 => mu perp nu (via thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion) is not written, so the failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' holds for this case.

ED26-P15-CH-density-martingales-and-product-measures-C013 (partial): The construction or argument and the full treatment promised by proved=annex:p15.product-bernoulli-boundaries are missing for two conclusions promised at body l.262-265. The annex (l.397-400) cites only 'the affinity summability criterion' (thm:p15-product-affinity-series), which yields mu<<nu iff sum eps_m^2<infinity. (i) The reverse direction nu<<mu is neither argued nor cited, yet 'The laws are equivalent exactly when sum eps_m^2<infinity' and 'eps_m=1/(4m) gives equivalence' both need it. The proof never states that Bernoulli coordinates with p_m,q_m in (0,1) are equivalent, and never appeals to the reverse-measure part of thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion. (ii) The claimed singularity for eps_m=1/(4 sqrt m) rests on the words 'giving the two examples', with no written step sum(1-h_m)=infinity => H_infinity=0 => mu perp nu. The failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' therefore holds.
